units.zh: 張文蔚，字右華，河間人也。
units.en: Zhang Wenyu, styled Youhua, came from Hejian.
units.literal: Zhang Wenyu, style Youhua, was a native of Hejian.

units.zh: 父裼，唐僖宗朝，累為顯官。
units.en: His father Ti rose through several high posts under Emperor Xizong of Tang.
units.literal: His father Ti, in Emperor Xizong's Tang, repeatedly held prominent offices.

units.zh: 文蔚幼礪文行，求知取友，藹然有佳士之稱。
units.en: From youth he cultivated letters and character, sought learning and worthy companions, and was known as a man of fine quality.
units.literal: As a youth Wenyu honed literary conduct, sought knowledge and chose friends, and was amiably styled an outstanding gentleman.

units.zh: 唐乾符初，登進士第，時丞相裴坦兼判鹽鐵，解褐署巡官。
units.en: In the early Qianfu era he took the jinshi degree; Chief Minister Pei Tan, who also oversaw the salt monopoly, gave him his first appointment as a patrol official.
units.literal: Early in Tang Qianfu he passed the jinshi; when Chief Minister Pei Tan concurrently administered the salt monopoly, he received his first appointment as a patrol official under him.

units.zh: 未幾，以畿尉直館。
units.en: Soon he served as a capital aide and was posted to the Hanlin archive.
units.literal: Before long he was made a capital-district aide and entered the Hanlin archive.

units.zh: 丁家艱，以孝聞。
units.en: When his father died, his mourning won wide praise.
units.literal: Upon his father's death he was famed for filial piety.

units.zh: 中和歲，僖宗在蜀，大寇未滅，急於軍費，移鹽鐵於揚州，命李都就判之，奏為轉運巡官。
units.en: During the Zhonghe reign, with the emperor in Shu and rebels still unchecked, the court moved salt administration to Yangzhou under Li Du; Wenyu was named transport patrol official.
units.literal: In the Zhonghe years, with Xizong in Shu, great bandits not yet destroyed, and military funds urgent, the salt monopoly was moved to Yangzhou; Li Du was ordered to administer it, and Wenyu was recommended as transport patrol official.

units.zh: 駕還長安，除監察御史，遷左補闕侍御史、起居舍人、司勳吏部員外郎，拜司勳郎中、知制誥，歲滿授中書舍人。
units.en: After the court returned to Chang'an he rose from supervising censor through remonstrator, attendant censor, and diarist to bureau director, then Merit Director and edict drafter; a year later he became Secretariat Drafter.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Chang'an, he was made supervising censor, then promoted through Left Remonstrator, attendant censor, diarist, and bureau registrars, appointed Director of Merit and drafter of edicts, and after a full year made Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 丁母憂，退居東畿，哀毀過禮。
units.en: He mourned his mother in the eastern suburbs, his grief so deep it outstripped the rites.
units.literal: Upon his mother's death he retired to the eastern capital suburbs, his grief exceeding ritual.

units.zh: 服闋，復拜中書舍人，俄召入翰林，為承旨學士。
units.en: After mourning he resumed as Secretariat Drafter and was soon called into the Hanlin as Academician Recipient of Edicts.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was again made Secretariat Drafter, soon summoned to the Hanlin as Academician Recipient of Edicts.

units.zh: 屬昭宗初還京闕，皇綱浸微，文蔚所發詔令，靡失厥中，論者多之。
units.en: When Zhaozong first came back to the capital, the throne was failing; Wenyu's edicts struck the right note every time, and men of judgment approved.
units.literal: As Zhaozong first returned to the capital, imperial governance grew weak; the edicts Wenyu drafted never missed the mark, and critics praised him.

units.zh: 轉戶部侍郎，仍依前充職，尋出為禮部侍郎。
units.en: He became Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining his old duties, then moved to Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue while keeping his former duties, then sent out as Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 天祐元年夏，拜中書侍郎、平章事，兼判戶部。
units.en: In summer of Tianyou 1 he was made Secretariat Vice Minister, Chief Councillor, and put in charge of Revenue.
units.literal: In the summer of the first year of Tianyou he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Chief Councillor, and concurrently administered Revenue.

units.zh: 時柳璨在相位，擅權縱暴，傾陷賢俊，宰相裴樞等五家及三省而下三十餘人，鹹抱冤就死；
units.en: Liu Can then dominated the court, abused power, and destroyed the worthy: Chancellor Pei Shu and four other families, with more than thirty men from the Three Departments, all died unjustly.
units.literal: At that time Liu Can held the chancellery, usurped power and ran wild, crushed worthy men—the chancellor Pei Shu and four other households plus more than thirty from the Three Departments all died innocent.

units.zh: 縉紳以目，不敢竊語其是非，餘怒所注，亦不啻十許輩。
units.en: Officials watched in silence, afraid even to murmur judgment; a dozen more still lay in the path of his rage.
units.literal: The gentry watched with their eyes and dared not whisper right from wrong; those still in his wrath numbered no fewer than ten-odd.

units.zh: 文蔚殫其力解之，乃止，士人賴焉。
units.en: Wenyu spent himself to halt the slaughter, and the scholarly class owed him their lives.
units.literal: Wenyu exhausted his strength to save them and stopped it; scholars relied on him.

units.zh: 璨敗死，文蔚兼度支鹽鐵使。
units.en: After Can's fall and death, Wenyu was also made Commissioner of Finance and Salt.
units.literal: When Can fell and died, Wenyu was made concurrent Commissioner of Finance and Salt.

units.zh: 天祐四年，天子以土運將革，天命有歸，四月，命文蔚與楊涉等總率百僚，奉禪位詔至大梁。
units.en: In Tianyou 4, believing the age of earth was ending and Heaven's mandate had turned, the emperor in the fourth month sent Wenyu and Yang She at the head of the bureaucracy to Daliang with the abdication edict.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tianyou the Son of Heaven, seeing the earthly cycle about to change and Heaven's mandate shifting, in the fourth month ordered Wenyu and Yang She to lead all officials bearing the abdication edict to Daliang.

units.zh: 太祖受命，文蔚等不易其位。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Wenyu and his colleagues kept their offices.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, Wenyu and the rest kept their posts.

units.zh: 開平二年春，暴卒於位，詔贈右僕射。
units.en: In spring of Kaiping 2 he died suddenly at his post; the court posthumously made him Right Vice Director.
units.literal: In the spring of the second year of Kaiping he died suddenly in office; an edict posthumously made him Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 文蔚沈邃重厚，有大臣之風，居家孝且悌，雖位至清顯，與仲季相雜，在太夫人膝下，一不異布素。
units.en: Deep, grave, and weighty, he bore a great minister's air; at home he was filial and fraternal. Though he had risen to the highest offices, he sat among his brothers at their mother's knee like any man in plain cloth.
units.literal: Wenyu was deep, withdrawn, and weighty, with a great minister's bearing; at home he was filial and brotherly—though his rank reached the highest clarity, he mingled with his brothers at their mother's knee no differently from common cloth.

units.zh: 弟濟美，早得心恙，
units.en: His brother Jimo had long suffered a disorder of the heart,
units.literal: His brother Jimo early suffered a heart ailment,

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：張裼尚書有五子：文蔚、彝憲、濟美、仁龜，皆有名第，至宰輔丞郎。
units.en: (The 《Northern Dreams Miscellany》 says Minister Zhang Ti had five sons—Wenyu, Yixian, Jimo, and Renqi—all earned degrees and rose to chancellor or bureau chief.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Scattered Words from Northern Dreams》 says: Minister Zhang Ti had five sons—Wenyu, Yixian, Jimo, and Renqi—all held famous degrees and reached chancellors and bureau directors.)〉

units.zh: 內一子，忘其名，少年聞壁魚食神仙字，身有五色，吞之可得仙，因欲試之，遂致心疾。
units.en: A fifth son, whose name is lost, heard as a boy that silverfish that eat sacred script turn five-colored and grant immortality if eaten; he tried it and lost his mind.
units.literal: One son, whose name is forgotten, in youth heard that booklice eating immortal characters turn five-colored and that swallowing them brings immortality; wishing to test it, he brought on a disorder of the heart.

units.zh: 是得急者別自一人非濟美也。）〉
units.en: The afflicted son was another brother, not Jimo.)〉
units.literal: The one who fell ill was a different person, not Jimo.)〉

units.zh: 文蔚撫視殆三十年，士君子稱之。
units.en: Wenyu tended him for nearly thirty years, to the praise of all who knew them.
units.literal: Wenyu cared for him nearly thirty years; gentlemen praised this.

units.zh: 子鑄，周顯德中，位至秘書監。
units.en: His son Zhuo rose to Director of the Palace Library under Later Zhou in the Xiande era.
units.literal: His son Zhuo, in Later Zhou Xiande, reached Director of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 薛貽矩，字熙用，河東聞喜人。
units.en: Xue Yiju, styled Xiyong, came from Wenxi in Hedong.
units.literal: Xue Yiju, style Xiyong, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.

units.zh: 祖存，父廷望，咸有令名。
units.en: His grandfather Cun and his father Tingwang both enjoyed excellent names.
units.literal: His grandfather Cun and father Tingwang both had fine reputations.

units.zh: 貽矩風儀秀聳，其與遊者皆一時英妙，藉甚於文場間。
units.en: Yiju stood tall in grace and presence; his circle held the brightest men of the day, and the literary world held him in high regard.
units.literal: Yiju's bearing was elegant and lofty; those who associated with him were all the finest of the age, and he was greatly esteemed in literary circles.

units.zh: 唐乾符中，登進士第，曆度支巡官、集賢校理、拾遺、殿中、起居舍人，召拜翰林學士，加禮部員外郎、知制誥，轉司勳郎中，其職如故。
units.en: He took the jinshi in Qianfu and moved through finance patrol work, Collegiate Reviser, remonstrator, palace and diarist posts, then Hanlin academician, Vice Director of Rites and edict drafter, and Director of Merit without changing his core duties.
units.literal: In Tang Qianfu he passed the jinshi and served in succession as finance patrol official, Collegiate Reviser, remonstrator, palace and diarist posts, was summoned as Hanlin academician, made Vice Director of Rites and edict drafter, transferred to Director of Merit, his duties unchanged.

units.zh: 乾寧中，天子幸石門，貽矩以私屬相失，不及於行在，罷之。
units.en: In Qianning, when the emperor went to Shimen, Yiju lost touch with his household train, failed to reach the traveling court, and was removed.
units.literal: In Qianning the Son of Heaven went to Shimen; Yiju, separated from his private entourage, did not reach the mobile court and was dismissed.

units.zh: 旋除中書舍人，再踐內署。
units.en: He was soon made Secretariat Drafter and returned to the inner secretariat.
units.literal: Soon he was made Secretariat Drafter and again entered the inner secretariat.

units.zh: 曆戶部兵部侍郎、學士承旨。
units.en: He went on to serve as Vice Minister of Revenue and War and as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
units.literal: He served in succession as Vice Minister of Revenue and War and as Academician Recipient of Edicts.

units.zh: 及昭宗自鳳翔還京，大翦閹寺，貽矩尚為韓全誨等作畫讚，悉記於內侍省屋壁間，坐是謫官。
units.en: When Zhaozong returned from Fengxiang and purged the eunuchs, Yiju was found to have painted laudatory portraits for Han Quanhui and others on the inner-service walls and was demoted.
units.literal: When Zhaozong returned from Fengxiang to the capital and greatly purged the eunuchs, Yiju had still painted encomia for Han Quanhui and others, all recorded on the walls of the inner service bureau, and for this was demoted.

units.zh: 天祐初，除吏部侍郎，不至。
units.en: Early in Tianyou he was named Vice Minister of Personnel but never reported.
units.literal: Early in Tianyou he was made Vice Minister of Personnel but did not take office.

units.zh: 太祖素重之，嘗言之於朝，即日拜吏部尚書，俄遷御史大夫。
units.en: The Founding Emperor had long esteemed him, mentioned him at court, and that day named him Minister of Personnel; soon after he became Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor had long valued him and once spoke of him at court; that same day he was made Minister of Personnel, and soon promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 四年春，唐帝命貽矩持詔赴大梁，議禪代之事。
units.en: In spring of the fourth year the Tang emperor sent Yiju to Daliang with the edict to negotiate abdication.
units.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Tang emperor ordered Yiju to carry the edict to Daliang to discuss the transfer of the mandate.

units.zh: 貽矩至，盛稱太祖功德，請就北面之禮，太祖雖謙抑不納，待之甚厚。
units.en: On arrival he extolled the Founding Emperor and urged him to accept the ceremony of a northern vassal; the emperor demurred but received him with great favor.
units.literal: When Yiju arrived he lavishly praised the Founding Emperor's merit and asked that he accept the rites of a northern subject; though the Founding Emperor modestly refused, he treated him very generously.

units.zh: 受禪之歲夏五月，拜中書侍郎、平章事，兼判戶部。
units.en: In the fifth month of the founding year he became Secretariat Vice Minister, Chief Councillor, and overseer of Revenue.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the year the mandate was received he was made Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Chief Councillor, and concurrently administered Revenue.

units.zh: 明年夏，進拜門下侍郎、監修國史，判度支，又遷宏文館大學士，充鹽鐵轉運使，累官自僕射至守司空。
units.en: The following summer he rose to Chancellery Vice Minister, supervised the national history, ran finance, became Grand Academician of Hongwen, Salt Transport Commissioner, and climbed from Vice Director to Acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: The next summer he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Chancellery, supervised compilation of the national history, administered finance, was made Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Salt Transport Commissioner, and rose in rank from Vice Director to Acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 在任綿五載，然亦無顯赫事跡可紀。
units.en: He served five full years, but left no deeds worth recording.
units.literal: He held office fully five years, yet no striking deeds are recorded.

units.zh: 扈從貝州還，染時癘，旬日卒於東京。
units.en: On the return from Beizhou he contracted an epidemic and died in the Eastern Capital within ten days.
units.literal: Returning from an expedition to Beizhou he caught an epidemic malady and died in the Eastern Capital within ten days.

units.zh: 詔贈侍中。
units.en: The court posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
units.literal: An edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 張策，字少逸，敦煌人。
units.en: Zhang Ce, styled Shaoyi, came from Dunhuang.
units.literal: Zhang Ce, style Shaoyi, was a native of Dunhuang.

units.zh: 父同，仕唐，官至容管經略使。
units.en: His father Tong served Tang and rose to Military Commissioner of Rongguan.
units.literal: His father Tong served Tang and reached Military Commissioner of Rongguan.

units.zh: 策少聰警好學，尤樂章句。
units.en: As a boy Ce was quick-witted and studious, with a special love of chapter-and-verse learning.
units.literal: Ce in youth was clever and fond of learning, especially delighting in chapter-and-phrase study.

units.zh: 居洛陽敦化裏，嘗浚甘泉井，得古鼎，耳有篆字曰：「魏黃初元年春二月，匠吉千」，且又製作奇巧，同甚寶之。
units.en: In Dunhua Lane, Luoyang, he dredged the Sweet Spring well and found an ancient tripod inscribed in seal script: "Huangchu year 1, spring, second month, artisan Ji Qian." The work was exquisitely wrought, and Tong prized it.
units.literal: Living in Dunhua Lane in Luoyang, he once dredged the Sweet Spring well and obtained an ancient tripod whose ears bore seal script: "First year of Huangchu, spring, second month, craftsman Ji Qian"—and its workmanship was marvelously ingenious; Tong treasured it greatly.

units.zh: 策時在父旁，徐言曰：「建安二十五年，曹公薨，改年為延康，其年十月，文帝受漢禪，始號黃初，則是黃初元年無二月明矣。
units.en: Standing beside his father, Ce said quietly, "In Jian'an 25 Cao Cao died and the era became Yan'kang; in the tenth month of that year Emperor Wen accepted Han's abdication and first used Huangchu—so Huangchu year 1 plainly had no second month.
units.literal: Ce was then at his father's side and said slowly: "In the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an Cao Gong died and the era was changed to Yan'kang; in the tenth month of that year Emperor Wen received Han's abdication and first took the name Huangchu—so clearly Huangchu year 1 had no second month.

units.zh: 鼎文何謬歟！」
units.en: The inscription on this vessel is wrong!"
units.literal: How erroneous is the tripod's inscription!"

units.zh: 同大驚，亟遣啟書室，取《魏志》展讀，一不失所啟，宗族奇之，時年十三。
units.en: Tong was astonished, had the study opened, and sent for the 《Records of Wei》—every detail matched. The clan was amazed; Ce was thirteen.
units.literal: Tong was greatly startled, hurriedly sent someone to open the study, fetch the 《Records of Wei》, and read—nothing missed from what Ce had said; the clan marveled at him; he was then thirteen.

units.zh: 然而妙通因果，酷奉空教，未弱冠，落發為僧，居雍之慈恩精廬，頗有高致。
units.en: Yet he was drawn to karma and devoted to Buddhism; before coming of age he tonsured and lived at Cien Monastery in Yong, cultivating a refined detachment.
units.literal: Yet he was finely versed in cause and effect and ardently followed the Empty Teaching; before his weak cap he shaved his head as a monk and lived at Cien Monastery in Yong, with quite a lofty air.

units.zh: 唐廣明末，大盜犯闕，策遂返初服，奉父母逃難，君子多之。
units.en: When bandits took the capital at the end of Guangming, he put off his robes, fled with his parents, and won praise from men of principle.
units.literal: At the end of Tang Guangming great bandits breached the capital; Ce then returned to lay dress, escorted his parents in flight, and gentlemen praised him.

units.zh: 及丁家艱，以孝聞。
units.en: When his father died, his mourning was widely praised.
units.literal: Upon his father's death he was famed for filial piety.

units.zh: 服滿，自屏郊藪，一無幹進意，若是者十餘載，方出為廣文博士，改秘書郎。
units.en: After mourning he hid in the countryside without seeking office for more than ten years, then took up posts as National University erudite and Secretary.
units.literal: When mourning ended he secluded himself in the wilds with no thought of advancement for more than ten years, then emerged as Erudite of the National University and was changed to Secretary.

units.zh: 王行瑜帥邠州，辟為觀察支使，帶水曹員外郎，賜緋。
units.en: Wang Xingyu of Binzhou made him observation aide and Water Bureau Registrar and gave him crimson robes.
units.literal: Wang Xingyu commanded Bin prefecture and recruited him as observation aide, with concurrent Water Bureau Registrar, and granted crimson.

units.zh: 及行瑜反，太原節度使李克用奉詔討伐，行瑜敗死，邠州平。
units.en: When Xingyu rebelled, Li Keyong of Taiyuan marched under imperial orders; Xingyu was defeated and killed, and Binzhou was pacified.
units.literal: When Xingyu rebelled, Taiyuan Military Commissioner Li Keyong received the edict to campaign; Xingyu was defeated and died, and Binzhou was pacified.

units.zh: 策與婢肩輿其親，南出邠境，屬邊寨積雪，為行者所哀。
units.en: Ce bore his family south from Bin in a litter borne with a servant girl; snow blocked the frontier posts, and passersby wept for them.
units.literal: Ce carried his kin in a shoulder litter with a maid south of Bin, and because border forts were deep in snow travelers pitied them.

units.zh: 太祖聞而嘉之，奏為鄭滑支使，尋以內憂去職。
units.en: The Founding Emperor heard and praised him, had him named aide to Zheng-Hua, and soon he left for mourning at home.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor heard and commended this, memorialized him as Zheng-Hua aide, and soon he left office for domestic mourning.

units.zh: 製闋，除國子博士，遷膳部員外郎。
units.en: After mourning he became National University erudite, then Registrar of the Provisions Bureau.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was made National University erudite and promoted to Bureau Registrar of Provisions.

units.zh: 不一歲，華帥韓建辟為判官，及建領許州，又為掌記。
units.en: Within a year Han Jian of Hua recruited him as judge; when Jian took Xuzhou, Ce became his recorder.
units.literal: Within a year Hua Military Commissioner Han Jian recruited him as judge; when Jian took Xuzhou, Ce again served as recorder.

units.zh: 天復中，策奉其主書幣來聘，太祖見而喜曰：「張夫子且至矣。」
units.en: In Tianfu, Ce came on embassy with his lord's letter and gifts; the Founding Emperor rejoiced and said, "Master Zhang is on his way."
units.literal: In Tianfu, Ce brought his lord's letter and gifts on a mission; the Founding Emperor on seeing him rejoiced and said: "Master Zhang is coming."

units.zh: 即奏為掌記，兼賜金紫。
units.en: He was at once named recorder and given gold and purple insignia.
units.literal: At once he was memorialized as recorder and also granted gold and purple.

units.zh: 天祐初，表其才，拜職方郎中，兼史館修撰，俄召入為翰林學士，轉兵部郎中，知制誥，依前修史。
units.en: Early in Tianyou his talent was recommended; he became Appointments Director and Historiographer, entered the Hanlin, became War Director and edict drafter, and kept compiling history.
units.literal: Early in Tianyou he was recommended for talent, made Bureau Director of Appointments and concurrent Historiographer, soon summoned to the Hanlin, transferred to Bureau Director of War and edict drafter, still compiling history.

units.zh: 未幾，遷中書舍人，職如故。
units.en: Soon he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter with the same duties.
units.literal: Before long he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, duties unchanged.

units.zh: 太祖受禪，改工部侍郎，加承旨。
units.en: At the founding Ce became Vice Minister of Works and Hanlin Expositor.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, Ce was made Vice Minister of Works and Expositor.

units.zh: 其年冬，轉禮部侍郎。
units.en: That winter he moved to Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: That winter he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 明年，從征至澤州，拜刑部侍郎、平章事，仍判戶部，尋遷中書侍郎。
units.en: The next year, on campaign at Zezhou, he became Punishments Vice Minister and Chief Councillor, still overseeing Revenue, then Secretariat Vice Minister.
units.literal: The next year, on campaign to Ze prefecture, he was made Vice Minister of Punishments, Chief Councillor, still administering Revenue, and soon promoted to Secretariat Vice Minister.

units.zh: 以風恙拜章乞骸，改刑部尚書致仕。
units.en: Ill with wind disorder, he asked to retire and was made Minister of Punishments in retirement.
units.literal: Because of wind ailment he memorialized begging to retire bones and was changed to Minister of Punishments, retired.

units.zh: 即日肩輿歸洛，居於福善裏，修篁嘉木，圖書琴酒，以自適焉。
units.en: The same day he went home to Luoyang in a litter, settling in Fushan Lane among bamboo, fine trees, books, wine, and zither.
units.literal: That same day he returned to Luoyang in a shoulder litter, living in Fushan Lane amid fine bamboo, good trees, books, zither, and wine, to suit himself.

units.zh: 乾化二年秋，卒。
units.en: He died in autumn of Qianhua 2.
units.literal: In autumn of the second year of Qianhua he died.

units.zh: 所著《典議》三卷、詞製歌詩二十卷、箋表三十卷，存於其家。
units.en: His writings—three fascicles of 《Canonical Discussions》, twenty of verse and songs, thirty of memorials—remain with his family.
units.literal: His works—the three fascicles of 《Canonical Discussions》, twenty fascicles of regulated compositions, songs, and poems, and thirty fascicles of memorials and reports—remain in his household.

units.zh: 杜曉，字明遠，京兆杜陵人。
units.en: Du Xiao, styled Mingyuan, came from Duling in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Du Xiao, style Mingyuan, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 祖審權，仕唐，位至宰相。
units.en: His grandfather Shenquan served Tang and rose to chancellor.
units.literal: His grandfather Shenquan served Tang and reached chancellor.

units.zh: 父讓能，官至守太尉、平章事。
units.en: His father Rangneng rose to Acting Grand Preceptor and Chief Councillor.
units.literal: His father Rangneng reached Acting Grand Preceptor and Chief Councillor.

units.zh: 乾寧中，邠、鳳二鎮舉兵犯王畿，讓能被其誣陷，天子不得已，賜死於臨皋驛。
units.en: In Qianning the Bin and Feng commands marched on the capital; Rangneng was framed, and the emperor, powerless, had him executed at Lingao post.
units.literal: In Qianning the Bin and Feng two commands raised troops against the capital region; Rangneng was slandered by them, and the Son of Heaven, having no choice, ordered his death at Lingao post station.

units.zh: 曉居喪柴立，幾至滅性。
units.en: In mourning Xiao stood rigid as a post, nearly wasting away.
units.literal: Xiao in mourning stood like firewood, nearly destroying his life.

units.zh: 憂滿，服幅巾七升，沈跡自廢者將十餘載。
units.en: When mourning ended he wore plain cloth and lived in seclusion for nearly ten years.
units.literal: When grief ended he wore a seven-sheng coarse headcloth and buried himself in obscurity for nearly ten years.

units.zh: 光化中，宰相崔允判鹽鐵，奏為巡官兼校書郎，尋除畿尉，直宏文館，皆不起。
units.en: In Guanghua, Chancellor Cui Yun, who ran the salt monopoly, named him patrol official and Proofreader, then capital aide at Hongwen—all of which he declined.
units.literal: In Guanghua Chancellor Cui Yun administered the salt monopoly and memorialized him as patrol official and concurrent Proofreader; soon he was made capital aide and posted to the Hongwen Hall—all posts he refused.

units.zh: 及昭宗東遷，宰相崔遠判戶部，又奏為巡官兼殿中丞。
units.en: When Zhaozong moved east, Chancellor Cui Yuan, overseeing Revenue, again named him patrol official and Palace Director.
units.literal: When Zhaozong moved east, Chancellor Cui Yuan administered Revenue and again memorialized him as patrol official and concurrent Palace Director.

units.zh: 或語之曰：「嵇中散死，子紹埋沒不自顯，山濤以物理勉之，乃仕。
units.en: Someone told him, "When Ji Kang died, his son Shao hid himself and would not serve; Shan Tao reasoned with him about the way of the world, and only then did he take office.
units.literal: Someone said to him: "When Zhongsan Gentleman Ji Kang died, his son Shao buried himself in obscurity and would not show himself; Shan Tao urged him by the logic of things, and only then did he take office.

units.zh: 吾子忍令杜氏歲時以鋪席祭其先人，同匹庶乎！」
units.en: Will you let the Du family lay out mats for their ancestors like any common household?"
units.literal: Can you bear to let the Du clan year after year spread mats to sacrifice to their ancestors like commoners!"

units.zh: 曉乃就官。
units.en: At that Xiao accepted office.
units.literal: Xiao then took office.

units.zh: 未幾，拜左拾遺，尋召為翰林學士，轉膳部員外郎，依前充職。
units.en: Soon he became Left Remonstrator, entered the Hanlin, and became Provisions Registrar while keeping his old duties.
units.literal: Before long he was made Left Remonstrator, soon summoned to the Hanlin, transferred to Bureau Registrar of Provisions, his former duties unchanged.

units.zh: 及崔遠得罪，出守本官，居數月，以本官知制誥，俄又召為學士，遷郎中充職。
units.en: When Cui Yuan fell, he returned to his former post; months later he drafted edicts in that capacity, was recalled to the Hanlin, and promoted to Director.
units.literal: When Cui Yuan fell from grace he was sent out to his original post; after several months, with that post he drafted edicts, and soon was again summoned as academician and promoted to Director while retaining duty.

units.zh: 太祖受禪，拜中書舍人，職如故。
units.en: At the founding he became Secretariat Drafter with the same duties.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, he was made Secretariat Drafter, duties unchanged.

units.zh: 開平三年，轉工部侍郎，充承旨。
units.en: In Kaiping 3 he became Vice Minister of Works and Hanlin Expositor.
units.literal: In the third year of Kaiping he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and made Expositor.

units.zh: 明年秋，拜中書侍郎、平章事，仍判戶部。
units.en: The following autumn he became Secretariat Vice Minister, Chief Councillor, and still oversaw Revenue.
units.literal: The next autumn he was made Secretariat Vice Minister, Chief Councillor, still administering Revenue.

units.zh: 庶人友珪篡位，遷禮部尚書、平章事、集賢殿大學士，依前判戶部。
units.en: When Yougui seized the throne, he was made Minister of Rites, Chief Councillor, and Grand Academician of Jixian, still running Revenue.
units.literal: When the commoner Yougui usurped the throne, he was moved to Minister of Rites, Chief Councillor, and Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall, still administering Revenue.

units.zh: 及袁象先之討友珪，禁兵大縱，曉中重創而卒。
units.en: When Yuan Xiangxian moved against Yougui the palace guard rampaged; Xiao was badly wounded in the tumult and died.
units.literal: When Yuan Xiangxian attacked Yougui the palace guard ran wild; Xiao was gravely wounded among them and died.

units.zh: 末帝即位，詔贈右僕射。
units.en: The Last Emperor posthumously made him Right Vice Director.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 曉博瞻有詞藻，時論稱之。
units.en: Xiao was learned and eloquent; contemporaries praised his prose.
units.literal: Xiao was broadly learned and had a literary gift; critics praised him.

units.zh: 兄光乂，
units.en: His older brother Guangyi,
units.literal: His elder brother Guangyi,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》表：光乂，字啟之。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 genealogy gives Guangyi the style Qizhi.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 tables: Guangyi, style Qizhi.)〉

units.zh: 有心疹，厥疾每作，或溢喙縱詬，或揮梃追撲，曉事之愈恭，未嘗一日少怠。
units.en: suffered a disorder of the heart; when it seized him he would curse wildly or chase people with a staff—yet Xiao tended him with growing reverence and never slackened a single day.
units.literal: had a heart rash; whenever the ailment struck he would spew curses from his mouth or seize a staff and chase and beat; Xiao served him the more respectfully and never for a day slackened.

units.zh: 居兩製之重，祖述前載，甚得王言之體。
units.en: In charge of imperial edicts he followed the great models and mastered the kingly tone of court prose.
units.literal: Holding the weight of the Two Edicts, he followed earlier models and grasped the royal style of language very well.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：曉貌如削玉，有制誥之才。）〉
units.en: (The 《Northern Dreams Miscellany》 says Xiao looked like carved jade and had a gift for edicts.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Scattered Words from Northern Dreams》 says: Xiao's appearance was like cut jade and he had the talent for edicts.)〉

units.zh: 及典秩尚書，志氣甚遠，一旦非分而沒，鹹冤惜焉。
units.en: As Minister of Rites his ambition ran far; then he died in the coup, and everyone mourned the wrong done him.
units.literal: When he reached Minister of Rites, his spirit was very far-reaching; in a single day he perished by usurpation, and all pitied the injustice.

units.zh: 豈三世為相，道忌太盛歟！
units.en: Had three generations as chancellor provoked the Way's hatred of excess?
units.literal: Was it that three generations as chancellor—the Way dislikes excessive prosperity?

units.zh: 敬翔，字子振，同州馮翊人。
units.en: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, came from Fengyi in Tongzhou.
units.literal: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Fengyi in Tongzhou.

units.zh: 唐神龍中平陽王暉之後也。
units.en: He claimed descent from Tang's Prince of Pingyang, Hui, of the Shenlong reign.
units.literal: He was a descendant of Prince of Pingyang Hui of the Shenlong era of Tang.

units.zh: 曾祖琬，綏州刺史。
units.en: His great-grandfather Wan was prefect of Sui.
units.literal: Great-grandfather Wan was prefect of Sui prefecture.

units.zh: 祖忻，同州掾。
units.en: His grandfather Xin was an aide in Tong prefecture.
units.literal: Grandfather Xin was an aide in Tong prefecture.

units.zh: 父袞，集州刺史。
units.en: His father Gun was prefect of Ji.
units.literal: Father Gun was prefect of Ji prefecture.

units.zh: 翔好讀書，尤長刀筆，應用敏捷。
units.en: Xiang loved learning, excelled at dispatch work, and wrote with quick facility.
units.literal: Xiang loved books, was especially skilled at administrative writing, and applied himself with quick wit.

units.zh: 乾符中，舉進士不第。
units.en: During Qianfu he failed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: In Qianfu he sat for the jinshi examination and failed.

units.zh: 及黃巢陷長安，乃東出關。
units.en: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an he fled east through the pass.
units.literal: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, he went east out through the pass.

units.zh: 時太祖初鎮大梁，有觀察支使王發者，翔里人也，翔往依焉，發以故人遇之，然無由薦達。
units.en: The Founder had just begun to hold Daliang; Wang Fa of his home district served as an observation aide, and Xiang attached himself to him; Fa received him as an old friend but could not get him a post.
units.literal: At that time the Founder had just taken command at Daliang; there was observation commissioner aide Wang Fa, a townsman of Xiang's; Xiang went to depend on him; Fa treated him as an old acquaintance, yet had no way to recommend him.

units.zh: 翔久之計窘，乃與人為箋刺，往往有警句，傳於軍中。
units.en: His prospects long bleak, Xiang drafted letters and memorials for hire; his sharp phrases spread through the camps.
units.literal: After long time Xiang's plans grew desperate; he then wrote letters and memorials for others, often with striking lines, and they circulated in the army.

units.zh: 太祖比不知書，章檄喜淺近語，聞翔所作，愛之，謂發曰：「知公鄉人有才，可與俱來。」
units.en: The Founder barely read; he liked proclamations in plain speech; when he heard Xiang's writing he was delighted and told Fa: "Your townsman has talent—bring him with you."
units.literal: The Founder had never known books; in proclamations he liked plain, near language; hearing what Xiang wrote, he loved it and said to Fa: "I learn your townsman has talent—he may come with you."

units.zh: 及見，應對稱旨，即補右職，每令從軍。
units.en: At their meeting Xiang answered to his liking; he was given a military post and kept at campaign.
units.literal: When he met him, his replies suited the intent; he was at once given a right-wing post and always ordered to follow the army.

units.zh: 翔不喜武職，求補文吏，即署館驛巡官，俾專掌檄奏。
units.en: Xiang disliked soldiering and asked for a clerkship; he was made post-station patrol officer in charge of proclamations and memorials.
units.literal: Xiang disliked military office, sought a civil clerk post, and was appointed post-station patrol officer, made solely to handle proclamations and memorials.

units.zh: 太祖與蔡賊相拒累歲，城門之外，戰聲相聞，機略之間，翔頗預之。
units.en: For years the Founder fought the Cai rebels; battle echoed outside the walls, and Xiang took a large share in planning.
units.literal: The Founder opposed the Cai bandits for many years; beyond the city gates battle sounds were heard; in stratagems Xiang took considerable part.

units.zh: 太祖大悅，恨得翔之晚，故軍謀政術，一以諮之。
units.en: The Founder rejoiced that he had found Xiang so late and consulted him on every military and civil matter.
units.literal: The Founder greatly rejoiced, regretted finding Xiang so late; hence military plans and government methods he consulted Xiang on all alike.

units.zh: 蔡賊平，奏授太子中允，賜緋。
units.en: After the Cai rebels were crushed he was made Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and given crimson robes.
units.literal: When the Cai bandits were pacified, he was memorialized and appointed Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and given crimson robe.

units.zh: 從平兗、鄆，改檢校水部郎中。
units.en: After Yan and Yun were pacified he became honorary Director of the Water Ministry.
units.literal: Following the pacification of Yan and Yun, he was changed to honorary Director of the Water Ministry bureau.

units.zh: 太祖兼鎮淮南，授揚府左司馬，賜金紫。
units.en: When the Founder also governed Huainan he was made Left Assistant Administrator of Yangzhou and given gold and purple.
units.literal: When the Founder also held Huainan, he was appointed Left Assistant Administrator of Yang prefecture and given gold and purple.

units.zh: 乾寧中，改光祿少卿充職。
units.en: In Qianning he was made Vice Director of the Court for the Imperial Sacrifices while keeping his duties.
units.literal: In Qianning he was changed to Vice Director of the Court for the Imperial Sacrifices while filling his post.

units.zh: 天復中，授檢校禮部尚書，遙領蘇州刺史。
units.en: In Tianfu he was made honorary Minister of Rites and titular prefect of Suzhou.
units.literal: In Tianfu he was appointed honorary Minister of Rites and held Suzhou prefect concurrently at a distance.

units.zh: 昭宗自岐下還長安，禦延喜樓，召翔與李振登樓勞問，翔授檢校右僕射、太府卿，賜號迎鑾協讚功臣。
units.en: When Zhaozong returned from Qi to Chang'an he went up Ascending Bliss Tower and summoned Xiang and Li Zhen to honor them; Xiang was made honorary Right Vice Director and Grand Treasurer with the title Meritorious Worthy Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage and Assists in Praise.
units.literal: Zhaozong returned from Qi to Chang'an, ascended Ascending Bliss Tower, summoned Xiang and Li Zhen to the tower to reward them with inquiry; Xiang was appointed honorary Right Vice Director, Grand Treasurer, and given the title Meritorious Worthy Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage and Assists in Praise.

units.zh: 太祖受禪，自宣武軍掌書記、前太府卿，授檢校司空，依前太府卿勾當宣徽院事。
units.en: At the Founder's accession, from chief secretary of the Xuanwu army and former Grand Treasurer he became honorary Minister of Works and still oversaw the Palace Domestic office as Grand Treasurer.
units.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, from Xuanwu Army chief secretary and former Grand Treasurer he was appointed honorary Minister of Works and continued as Grand Treasurer to oversee Palace Domestic matters.

units.zh: 尋改樞密院為崇政院，以翔知院事。
units.en: Soon the Privy Council became the Chongzheng Court, with Xiang in charge of its affairs.
units.literal: Soon the Privy Council was changed to the Chongzheng Court and Xiang was made to know its affairs.

units.zh: 開平三年夏四月，太祖以邠、岐侵擾，遣劉知俊西討鄜、延，深憂不濟，因宴顧翔，以問西事。
units.en: In the fourth month of summer, Kaiping 3, with Bin and Qi raiding, the Founder sent Liu Zhijun west against Fu and Yan; deeply worried, he turned to Xiang at a banquet to ask about the western front.
units.literal: Kaiping year 3, fourth month of summer: the Founder because Bin and Qi were harrying sent Liu Zhijun west to attack Fu and Yan, deeply feared failure, and at a banquet turned to Xiang to ask about western affairs.

units.zh: 翔剖析山川郡邑虛實，軍糧多少，悉以條奏，如素講習，左右莫不驚異，太祖歎賞久之。
units.en: Xiang laid out terrain, prefectures, supplies, and strength in ordered detail as if he had long studied them; the court was astonished and the Founder marveled at length.
units.literal: Xiang analyzed mountains and rivers, prefectures and counties—their emptiness or substance, army grain—how much; all he submitted in items, as if he had long studied it; those on left and right were all astonished; the Founder sighed in admiration a long while.

units.zh: 乾化元年，進位光祿大夫，行兵部尚書、金鑾殿大學士，知崇政院事、平陽郡侯。
units.en: In Qianhua 1 he rose to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of War, Grand Academician of the Golden Hall, director of the Chongzheng Court, and Marquis of Pingyang.
units.literal: Qianhua year 1: he advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of War, Grand Academician of the Golden Hall, knowing Chongzheng Court affairs, Marquis of Pingyang commandery.

units.zh: 前朝因金巒坡以為門名，與翰林院相接，故得為學士者稱「金巒」以美之，今殿名「金鑾」，從嘉名也。
units.en: The former court had named its gate for Jinluan slope beside the Hanlin Academy, so academicians were styled "Jinluan" in praise; the hall was now named "Jinluan" after that auspicious usage.
units.literal: The previous dynasty took Jinluan slope as the gate name; it adjoined the Hanlin Academy; therefore those who became academicians were called "Jinluan" as a compliment; now the hall name is "Jinluan"—following the auspicious name.

units.zh: 置大學士，始以翔為之。
units.en: The office of Grand Academician was created, and Xiang was the first appointee.
units.literal: The grand academician office was established; Xiang was first to hold it.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：以「金鑾」為名，非典也。
units.en: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》 says naming the hall "Jinluan" was not canonical.
units.literal: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》 says: taking "Jinluan" as the name is not canonical.

units.zh: 大學士與三館大學士同。）〉
units.en: The Grand Academician matched the Three Institutes Grand Academician.)〉
units.literal: The grand academician is the same as the Three Institutes grand academician.)〉

units.zh: 翔自釋褐東下，遭遇霸王，懷抱深沉，有經濟之略，起中和歲，至鼎革大運，其間三十餘年，扈從征伐，出入帷幄，庶務叢委，恒達旦不寢，惟在馬上稍得晏息。
units.en: From his first post eastward Xiang served a rising hegemon: deep, reserved, and skilled in statecraft. From Zhonghe to the dynastic change—more than thirty years—he campaigned at the Founder's side, entered and left the command tent, and was buried in affairs, often working until dawn and resting only in the saddle.
units.literal: From first office eastward down Xiang met a hegemon king; his bosom was deep and reserved, with economic strategy; from the Zhonghe year to the great turning of the mandate, more than thirty years within—he followed in campaigns, entered and left the tent curtain; common affairs piled thick; he always reached dawn without sleep, only on horseback slightly obtaining rest.

units.zh: 每有所裨讚，亦未嘗顯諫，上俯仰顧步間微示持疑爾，而太祖意已察，必改行之，故裨佐之跡，人莫得知。
units.en: When he wished to counsel he never spoke outright; a slight hesitation in the Founder's glance was enough, and the Founder would change course—so few knew how much he had shaped events.
units.literal: Whenever he could aid or praise, he also never remonstrated plainly; the sovereign in the interval of bowing and looking and pacing would lightly show doubt—and the Founder's intent already perceived, he would certainly change and act; therefore the traces of his assistance—no one could know.

units.zh: 及太祖大漸，召至御床前受顧托之命，且深以並寇為恨，翔鳴咽不忍，受命而退。
units.en: At the Founder's deathbed Xiang received his final charge; the Founder bitterly regretted the Jin foe; Xiang wept and withdrew, unable to bear it.
units.literal: When the Founder was gravely ill, Xiang was summoned to the imperial bedside to receive the entrusting command; and he (the Founder) deeply regretted the Jin enemy; Xiang sobbed and could not bear it; he received the mandate and withdrew.

units.zh: 庶人友珪之篡位也，以天下之望，命翔為宰相。
units.en: When the usurper Yougui seized the throne, public expectation made him name Xiang chancellor.
units.literal: When the commoner Yougui usurped the throne, by the hope of all under Heaven he ordered Xiang as chancellor.

units.zh: 友珪以翔先朝舊臣，有所畏忌，翔亦多稱病，不綜政事。
units.en: Yougui feared this holdover from the old court; Xiang often pleaded illness and stayed out of government.
units.literal: Yougui because Xiang was an old minister of the former court had some fear and caution; Xiang too often claimed illness and did not oversee government affairs.

units.zh: 末帝即位，趙、張之族皆處權要，翔愈不得志。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor the Zhao and Zhang families held power, and Xiang grew still more frustrated.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, the Zhao and Zhang clans all held crucial power; Xiang grew still more without satisfaction.

units.zh: 及劉鄩失河朔，安彥之喪楊劉，翔奏曰：「國家連年遣將出征，封疆日削，不獨兵驕將怯，亦製置未得其術。
units.en: After Liu Xun lost Hebei and An Yanzhi lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized: "Year after year we send armies abroad while our borders shrink—not only are the troops arrogant and the generals timid; our strategy is wrong as well.
units.literal: When Liu Xun lost Hebei, and An Yanzhi lost Yangliu, Xiang memorialized saying: "The state year after year sends generals on campaign; the borders daily shrink—not only are troops arrogant and generals timid; disposition too has not obtained its method.

units.zh: 陛下處深宮之中，與之計事者皆左右近習，豈能量敵之勝負哉！
units.en: Your Majesty sits deep in the palace while only favorites advise you—how can you judge the enemy's strength?
units.literal: Your Majesty dwells deep in the palace; those who plan affairs with you are all close attendants on left and right—how can one measure the enemy's victory or defeat!

units.zh: 先皇時，河朔半在，親禦虎臣驍將，猶不得志於敵人。
units.en: Under the late emperor half of Hebei was still ours; he led his best commanders in person and still could not beat the foe.
units.literal: In the late emperor's time, half of Hebei remained; he personally led tiger ministers and fierce generals—yet still could not satisfy his will upon the enemy.

units.zh: 今寇馬已至鄆州，陛下不留聖念，臣所未喻一也。
units.en: Now the enemy has reached Yunzhou while Your Majesty shows no alarm—that is what I cannot understand first.
units.literal: Now the enemy's horses have already reached Yun prefecture; Your Majesty does not keep sage concern—what I cannot understand is the first point.

units.zh: 臣聞李亞子自墨縗統眾，於今十年，每攻城臨陣，無不親當矢石，昨聞攻楊劉，率先負薪渡水，一鼓登城。
units.en: Li Yazi has led his men in mourning garb for ten years; in every siege he faces arrows and stones himself; at Yangliu he carried fuel to ford the river and took the city at the first drum.
units.literal: I hear Li Yazi from hemp mourning has commanded the masses—already ten years now; whenever he attacks cities and faces battle lines, there is none at which he does not personally meet arrows and stones; yesterday I heard attacking Yangliu, he first shouldered fuel to cross the water, and at one drum took the walls.

units.zh: 陛下儒雅守文，未嘗如此，俾賀瑰輩與之較力，而望攘逐寇戎，臣所未喻二也。
units.en: Your Majesty is a scholar-king who has never done such things, yet you send He Gui and others to match him and still hope to drive the invaders away—that is what I cannot understand second.
units.literal: Your Majesty is refined and cultured, guarding the written law, and has never been thus; you make He Gui and his ilk compare strength with him, yet hope to drive away and expel the enemy raiders—what I cannot understand is the second point.

units.zh: 陛下所宜詢於黎老，別運沉謀，不然，則憂未艾也。
units.en: You should consult seasoned elders and lay deeper plans—or our troubles will not end.
units.literal: What Your Majesty ought to do is consult the grey-haired elders and separately deploy deep strategy—otherwise worry will not end.

units.zh: 臣雖駑怯，受國恩深，陛下必若乏材，乞於邊陲效試。」
units.en: I am untalented but deeply in your debt; if you lack men, let me prove myself on the frontier."
units.literal: Though I am dull and timid, I have received the state's grace deeply; if Your Majesty must lack talent, I beg to be tried in effect at the frontier."

units.zh: 末帝雖知其懇惻，竟以趙、張輩言翔怨望，不之聽。
units.en: The Last Emperor knew he spoke sincerely, but Zhao and Zhang called it resentment, and he would not listen.
units.literal: The Last Emperor though he knew his earnest sincerity, in the end because the Zhao and Zhang crowd said Xiang harbored resentment, did not heed him.

units.zh: 及王彥章敗於中都，晉人長驅而南，末帝急召翔，謂之曰：「朕居常忽卿所奏，果至今日。
units.en: When Wang Yanzhang fell at Zhongdu and the Jin army swept south, the Last Emperor summoned Xiang in haste and said: "I ignored your warnings, and it has come to this.
units.literal: When Wang Yanzhang was defeated at Zhongdu, Jin men drove at length south; the Last Emperor urgently summoned Xiang and said to him: "I in ordinary times neglected what you memorialized—it has indeed come to this day.

units.zh: 事急矣，勿以為懟，且使朕安歸？」
units.en: Matters are desperate; do not be angry—where can I go in safety?"
units.literal: Matters are urgent; do not take it as offense—and where shall I return in peace?"

units.zh: 翔泣奏曰：「臣受國恩，僅將三紀，從微至著，皆先朝所遇，雖名宰相，實朱氏老奴耳。
units.en: Xiang wept and replied: "I have served nearly thirty years, raised from nothing by the former court; though called chancellor, I am only an old retainer of the Zhu house.
units.literal: Xiang wept and memorialized saying: "Your servant has received the state's grace for nearly three decades; from slight to manifest—all from the former court's encounter; though named chancellor, in truth I am the Zhu clan's old bondservant.

units.zh: 事陛下如郎君，以臣愚誠，敢有所隱！
units.en: I serve you as a young master would be served—with my poor loyalty I dare hide nothing!
units.literal: Serving Your Majesty like a young master—for your servant's dull sincerity, how dare I hide anything!

units.zh: 陛下初任段凝為將，臣已極言，小人朋附，致有今日。
units.en: When you first made Duan Ning commander I warned you to the utmost; petty factions brought us to this day.
units.literal: Your Majesty at first appointed Duan Ning as general—I already spoke to the limit; petty men banded together and brought about this day.

units.zh: 晉軍即至，段凝限水。
units.en: The Jin army is upon us, and Duan Ning is blocked by the river.
units.literal: The Jin army will soon arrive; Duan Ning is cut off by water.

units.zh: 欲請陛下出居避敵，陛下必不聽從；
units.en: If I urge you to leave the capital to escape the enemy, you will not listen;
units.literal: I wish to ask Your Majesty to go out and dwell to avoid the enemy—Your Majesty certainly will not obey;

units.zh: 欲請陛下出奇應敵，陛下必不果決。
units.en: if I urge a bold stroke against the enemy, you will not decide.
units.literal: I wish to ask Your Majesty to deploy surprise to answer the enemy—Your Majesty certainly will not in the end decide.

units.zh: 縱良、平復生，難以轉禍為福，請先死，不忍見宗廟隕墜。」
units.en: Even Zhang Liang and Chen Ping reborn could not turn this ruin to blessing; let me die first—I cannot watch the ancestral temples fall."
units.literal: Even if Liang and Ping were reborn, it would be hard to turn disaster into fortune; I beg to die first—I cannot bear to see the ancestral temples fall."

units.zh: 言訖，君臣相向慟哭。
units.en: They ended in tears together.
units.literal: When words ended, ruler and minister faced each other and wailed.

units.zh: 及晉主陷都城，有詔赦梁氏臣僚，李振謂翔曰：「有制洗滌，將朝新君。」
units.en: When the Jin took the capital an edict pardoned Liang officials; Li Zhen told Xiang: "We are absolved—we should attend the new court."
units.literal: When the Jin ruler took the capital, there was an edict pardoning Liang clan ministers and clerks; Li Zhen said to Xiang: "There is an edict to wash clean—we shall attend court before the new ruler."

units.zh: 翔曰：「新君若問，其將何辭以對！」
units.en: Xiang said: "If the new ruler questions us, what answer can we give?"
units.literal: Xiang said: "If the new ruler asks, with what words shall we reply!"

units.zh: 是夜，翔在高頭裏第，宿於車坊。
units.en: That night he stayed in the carriage house at his Gaotou Lane mansion.
units.literal: That night Xiang was at his Gaotou Lane residence, lodging in the carriage shed.

units.zh: 欲曙，左右報曰：「崇政李太保已入朝。」
units.en: Near dawn his attendants said: "Senior Guardian Li of the Chongzheng Court has already gone to court."
units.literal: Near dawn, attendants reported: "Chongzheng Court Senior Guardian Li has already entered court."

units.zh: 翔返室歎曰：「李振謬為丈夫耳！
units.en: Xiang went inside and sighed: "Li Zhen is no true man!
units.literal: Xiang returned to his room and sighed: "Li Zhen falsely calls himself a man!

units.zh: 朱氏與晉仇讎，我等始同謀畫，致君無狀，今少主伏劍於國門，縱新朝赦罪，何面目入建國門也！」
units.en: The Zhu house and Jin are mortal enemies; we plotted together and drove our lord to ruin; the young emperor died by the sword at the gate—even pardoned, how can we pass through Jianguo Gate!"
units.literal: The Zhu clan and Jin are mortal foes; we at first together plotted and counselled, causing our lord to act without restraint; now the young master fell by the sword at the state gate—even if the new court pardons crimes, with what face enter the Jianguo Gate!"

units.zh: 乃自經而卒。
units.en: He hanged himself.
units.literal: He then hanged himself and died.

units.zh: 數日，並其族被誅。
units.en: Days later his whole clan was executed.
units.literal: Within several days, together with his clan he was put to death.

units.zh: 初，貞明中，史臣李琪、張袞、郤殷象、馮錫嘉奉詔修撰《太祖實錄》三十卷，敘述非工，事多漏略。
units.en: Early in Zhenming, Li Qi, Zhang Gun, Xi Yinxiang, and Feng Xijia were ordered to compile thirty scrolls of the 《Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor》; the narrative was poor and much was left out.
units.literal: At the start, in Zhenming, historians Li Qi, Zhang Gun, Xi Yinxiang, and Feng Xijia received edict to compile the 《Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor》 thirty scrolls; the narration was unskilled and affairs were much omitted.

units.zh: 復詔翔補緝其闕，翔乃別纂成三十卷，目之曰《大梁編遺錄》，與《實錄》偕行。
units.en: Xiang was then ordered to fill the gaps; he compiled another thirty scrolls titled 《Compiled Remnant Records of Great Liang》, issued together with the 《Veritable Records》.
units.literal: Again an edict ordered Xiang to supplement and edit its gaps; Xiang then separately compiled into completion thirty scrolls, titled them 《Compiled Remnant Records of Great Liang》, and they circulated together with the 《Veritable Records》.

units.zh: 翔妻劉氏，父為藍田令。
units.en: Xiang's wife, Lady Liu, was daughter of the magistrate of Lantian.
units.literal: Xiang's wife, the Liu clan—her father was magistrate of Lantian.

units.zh: 廣明之亂，劉為巢將尚讓所得，巢敗，讓攜劉降於時溥，及讓誅，時溥納劉於妓室。
units.en: In the Guangming disorders she was seized by Huang Chao's general Shang Rang; after Chao's fall Rang surrendered her to Shi Pu, and when Rang was killed Pu kept her among his entertainers.
units.literal: In the Guangming turmoil Liu was taken by Huang Chao's general Shang Rang; when Chao was defeated, Rang brought Liu and surrendered to Shi Pu; when Rang was executed, Shi Pu took Liu into his courtesans' quarters.

units.zh: 太祖平徐，得劉氏嬖之，屬翔喪妻，因以劉氏賜之。
units.en: When the Founder took Xuzhou he favored Lady Liu; Xiang was widowed, and the Founder gave her to him.
units.literal: When the Founder pacified Xu, he obtained Lady Liu and favored her; as Xiang had lost his wife, he therefore gave Lady Liu to him.

units.zh: 及翔漸貴，劉猶出入太祖臥內，翔情禮稍薄，劉於曲室讓翔曰：「卿鄙餘曾失身於賊耶，以成敗言之，尚讓巢之宰輔，時溥國之忠臣，論卿門第，辱我何甚，請從此辭！」
units.en: As Xiang rose, Liu still visited the Founder's bedchamber; Xiang's affection cooled. In private she reproached him: "Do you scorn me for having served rebels? Shang Rang was Huang Chao's chancellor and Shi Pu a loyal minister of the state—and by your own birth, how deeply you insult me! I will leave you!"
units.literal: When Xiang gradually grew eminent, Liu still entered and left the Founder's sleeping quarters; Xiang's sentiment and courtesy grew somewhat thin; Liu in a side room reproached Xiang saying: "Sir, do you despise me because I once lost my integrity to bandits? Judging by success and failure—Shang Rang was Chao's chancellor, Shi Pu the state's loyal minister; considering your clan standing—how greatly you insult me! I beg to part from here!"

units.zh: 翔謝而止之。
units.en: Xiang apologized and kept her.
units.literal: Xiang apologized and stopped her.

units.zh: 劉恃太祖之勢，
units.en: Lady Liu relied on the Founder's favor,
units.literal: Liu relied on the Founder's power,

units.zh: 〈（案：下有缺文。）〉
units.en: (The text below is lost.)〉
units.literal: (Note: Below there is missing text.)〉

units.zh: 太祖四鎮時，劉已得「國夫人」之號。
units.en: While the Founder held four commands she already bore the title "State Lady."
units.literal: When the Founder held four commands, Liu already had the title "Lady of the State."

units.zh: 車服驕侈，婢媵皆珥珠翠，其下別置爪牙典謁，書幣聘使，交結藩鎮，近代婦人之盛，無出其右，權貴皆相附麗，寵信言事，不下於翔。
units.en: Her equipage was lavish, her maids jeweled; she kept her own agents and messengers and cultivated the frontier lords; no woman of the age matched her power; the great all courted her, and her influence rivaled Xiang's.
units.literal: Carriages and robes were arrogant and extravagant; maids and concubines all wore pearl and kingfisher in their ears; below her she separately set claw-and-tooth managers of audience; letters and gifts and envoys for betrothal—she linked with frontier commands; among women of recent ages none exceeded her on the right; power and nobility all attached to her; favor and trust in speaking affairs were not below Xiang.

units.zh: 當時貴達之家，從而效之，敗俗之甚也。
units.en: Great families imitated her—a grave debasement of manners.
units.literal: At that time eminent and reaching households followed and imitated her—a great corruption of custom.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：敬翔應《三傳》，數舉不第，發憤投太祖，願備行陣。
units.en: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says Xiang had studied the Three Commentaries, failed the exams repeatedly, and in anger joined the Founder, asking to serve in the ranks.
units.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Jing Xiang answered on the Three Commentaries, repeatedly sat for the examination without passing, in angry resolution threw himself on the Founder, willing to serve in the ranks.

units.zh: 太祖問曰：「足下通《春秋》久矣，今吾主盟，其為戰欲效春秋時可乎？」
units.en: The Founder asked: "You have long known the 《Spring and Autumn》; I now lead the alliance—should our wars follow the Spring and Autumn model?"
units.literal: The Founder asked: "You, sir, have long mastered the 《Spring and Autumn》; now I preside over the covenant—do you wish warfare to imitate Spring and Autumn times?"

units.zh: 翔曰：「不可。
units.en: Xiang said: "No.
units.literal: Xiang said: "It cannot be done.

units.zh: 夫禮樂猶不相沿襲，況兵者詭道，宜其變化無窮。
units.en: Even rites and music are not copied unchanged—how much more war, the art of deception, which must shift without limit.
units.literal: Rites and music still do not follow in succession—how much more warfare, the way of deception—fitly it changes without end.

units.zh: 若復如春秋時，則所謂務虛名而喪其實效，大王之事去矣。」
units.en: To fight like the Spring and Autumn age would chase empty form and lose real gain—your enterprise would fail."
units.literal: If again like Spring and Autumn times, then what is called pursuing empty names while losing real effect—my lord's enterprise is gone."

units.zh: 太祖大悅，以為知兵，遽延之幕府，委以軍事，竟至作相。）〉
units.en: The Founder was delighted, judged him a strategist, brought him into headquarters, entrusted him with military affairs, and in the end made him chancellor.)〉
units.literal: The Founder greatly rejoiced, considered him to know warfare, hastily extended him to the headquarters, entrusted him with military affairs, and in the end he reached chancellor.)〉

units.zh: 李振，字興緒，唐潞州節度使抱真之曾孫也。
units.en: Li Zhen, styled Xingxu, was great-grandson of Li Baozhen, Tang military commissioner of Lu.
units.literal: Li Zhen, styled Xingxu, was great-grandson of Tang's Li Baozhen, military commissioner of Lu prefecture.

units.zh: 祖、父，皆至郡守。
units.en: His grandfather and father both rose to commandery prefect.
units.literal: Grandfather and father both reached prefect of a commandery.

units.zh: 振仕唐，自金吾將軍改台州刺史。
units.en: He served Tang as a Golden Guard general, then became prefect of Taizhou.
units.literal: Zhen served Tang; from Golden Guard general he was changed to prefect of Tai prefecture.

units.zh: 會盜據浙東，不克之任，因西歸過汴，以策略幹太祖，太祖奇之，辟為從事。
units.en: Rebels held Zhedong and he could not take office; passing Bian on his return west he presented a plan to the Founder, who was impressed and took him on staff.
units.literal: As bandits held Zhedong, he could not reach his post; he therefore returned west passing Bian, with strategy approached the Founder; the Founder marveled at him and recruited him as staff officer.

units.zh: 太祖兼領鄆州，署天平軍節度副使。
units.en: When the Founder also held Yunzhou he made him deputy commissioner of the Tianping army.
units.literal: When the Founder also held Yun prefecture, he appointed him deputy military commissioner of Tianping army.

units.zh: 湖南馬殷為朗州雷滿所逼，振奉命馳往和解，殷、滿皆稟命。
units.en: When Ma Yin of Hunan was harried by Lei Man of Langzhou, Zhen was sent to mediate; both submitted.
units.literal: Hunan's Ma Yin was pressed by Langzhou's Lei Man; Zhen received command and galloped to mediate; Yin and Man both obeyed orders.

units.zh: 光啟三年十一月，太祖遣振入奏於長安，舍於州邸，邸吏程岩白振曰：「劉中尉命其侄希貞來計大事，欲上謁，願許之。」
units.en: In the eleventh month of Guangqi 3 the Founder sent Zhen to report at Chang'an; lodging at the circuit hostel, clerk Cheng Yan said: "Vice Director Liu has sent his nephew Xizhen to discuss a great matter and wishes an audience—will you allow it?"
units.literal: Guangqi year 3, eleventh month: the Founder sent Zhen to memorialize at Chang'an; he lodged at the prefecture residence; residence clerk Cheng Yan told Zhen: "Vice Director Liu ordered his nephew Xizhen to come to plan the great affair and wishes to pay court audience—may you permit it."

units.zh: 既至，岩乃先啟曰：「主上嚴急，內官憂恐，左中尉欲行廢黜之事，岩等協力以定中外，敢以事告。」
units.en: When Xizhen came, Yan announced: "The emperor is harsh; the eunuchs are afraid; the Left Vice Director means to depose him—we have joined forces to settle the realm and report this to you."
units.literal: When he arrived, Yan then first announced: "The sovereign is severe and urgent; inner officials are anxious and afraid; the Left Vice Director wishes to carry out deposition—Yan and others exert strength together to settle inner and outer; we dare report the affair."

units.zh: 振顧希貞曰：「百歲奴事三歲主，亂國不義，廢君不祥，非敢聞也。
units.en: Zhen told Xizhen: "An old servant plotting against a young lord is unrighteous; deposing the ruler is ill-omened—I will not hear of it.
units.literal: Zhen turned to Xizhen and said: "A hundred-year bondservant serving a three-year master—disordering the state is unrighteous, deposing the ruler is inauspicious; I dare not hear of it.

units.zh: 況梁王以百萬之師，匡輔天子，禮樂尊戴，猶恐不及，幸熟計之。」
units.en: The Prince of Liang leads a million men to aid the Son of Heaven in restoring rites and honor—he can scarcely do enough; think carefully."
units.literal: Moreover the Prince of Liang with a million troops aids and supports the Son of Heaven—rites and music, honored support—he still fears he does not reach it; I hope you will maturely plan."

units.zh: 希貞大沮而去。
units.en: Xizhen withdrew in dismay.
units.literal: Xizhen greatly dejected left.

units.zh: 及振復命，劉季述等果作亂，程岩率諸道邸吏牽帝下殿，以立幼主，奉昭宗為太上皇。
units.en: When Zhen returned, Liu Jishu and his party had rebelled; Cheng Yan and the hostel clerks of every circuit dragged the emperor from the hall, enthroned a child, and made Zhaozong Retired Emperor.
units.literal: When Zhen returned with his reply, Liu Jishu and others indeed made disorder; Cheng Yan led residence clerks of all circuits to drag the emperor down from the hall, set up the young ruler, and made Zhaozong Retired Emperor.

units.zh: 振至陝，陝已賀矣。
units.en: When Zhen reached Shaan, Shaan had already offered congratulations.
units.literal: Zhen reached Shaan; Shaan had already congratulated [the new ruler].

units.zh: 護軍韓彝範言其事，振曰：「懿皇初升遐，韓中尉殺長立幼，以利其權，遂亂天下，今將軍復欲爾耶！」
units.en: Protector-general Han Yifan raised the matter; Zhen said: "When Emperor Yizong died, Vice Director Han killed the elder prince and set up the younger for his own power and threw the realm into chaos—do you mean to do the same?"
units.literal: Protector-general Han Yifan spoke of the affair; Zhen said: "When Emperor Yizong first ascended to the far journey, Vice Director Han killed the elder and set up the young to profit his power—and so disordered all under Heaven; now General, do you again wish to do so!"

units.zh: 彝範即文約孫也，由是不敢言。
units.en: Yifan was Wenyao's grandson and dared not speak again.
units.literal: Yifan was Wenyao's grandson, and therefore dared not speak further.

units.zh: 振東歸，太祖方在邢、洺，遽還於汴，大計未決，季述遣養子希度以唐之社稷欲輸於太祖，又遣供奉官李奉本、副介支彥勳詐齎上皇誥諭至，皆季述黨也。
units.en: Zhen returned east while the Founder was at Xing and Ming and hurried back to Bian before policy was fixed; Liu Jishu sent his adopted son Xidu to hand Tang's realm to him, and Palace Attendant Li Fengben and Vice Messenger Zhi Yanxun with forged retired-emperor edicts—all Jishu's men.
units.literal: Zhen returned east; the Founder was then at Xing and Ming, hurried back to Bian, and the great plan was not yet settled; Jishu sent his adopted son Xidu to offer Tang's altars to the Founder, and also sent Palace Attendant Li Fengben and Vice Messenger Zhi Yanxun falsely bearing the Retired Emperor's edicts—all were Jishu's partisans.

units.zh: 太祖未及迎命，振又言曰：「夫豎貂、伊戾之亂，所以資霸者之事也。
units.en: Before the Founder could receive them, Zhen said again: "Rebellions like Shu Diao's and Yi Li's are what make a hegemon's career.
units.literal: Before the Founder could welcome the envoys, Zhen again said: "The disorders of Shu Diao and Yi Li are what supply a hegemon's affairs.

units.zh: 今閹豎幽辱天子，王不能討，無以令諸侯。」
units.en: Eunuchs now hold and humiliate the emperor; if you will not punish them, you cannot command the lords."
units.literal: Now eunuchs imprison and insult the Son of Heaven; if the King cannot punish them, you cannot command the feudal lords."

units.zh: 時監軍使劉重楚，季述兄也，舊相張浚，寓於河南緱氏，亦來謂太祖曰：「同中官則事易濟，且得所欲。」
units.en: Military inspector Liu Chongchu, Jishu's elder brother, and former chancellor Zhang Jun lodging at Gou in Henan also urged the Founder: "Side with the eunuchs and all goes easily—you get what you want."
units.literal: At that time military inspector Liu Chongchu, Jishu's elder brother, and former chief minister Zhang Jun lodging at Gou in Henan, also came to tell the Founder: "Join the inner attendants and affairs go easily, and you get what you want."

units.zh: 惟振堅執不改，獨曰：「行正道則大勳可立。」
units.en: Only Zhen held firm and said alone: "Follow the righteous way and great merit can be won."
units.literal: Only Zhen firmly held and would not change, alone saying: "Walk the upright path and great merit can be established."

units.zh: 太祖英悟，忽厲色曰：「張公勸我同敕使，欲傾附自求宰相耶！」
units.en: The Founder was sharp-witted; suddenly he said sternly: "Lord Zhang wants me to join the edict commissioners—are you angling to topple me and buy the chancellorship!"
units.literal: The Founder was keen-witted; suddenly with stern countenance he said: "Lord Zhang urges me to join the edict commissioners—do you wish to topple and attach yourself to seek the chancellorship!"

units.zh: 乃定策縶偽使李奉本、支彥勳與希度等，即日請振將命於京師，與宰相謀返正。
units.en: He bound the false envoys Li Fengben, Zhi Yanxun, and Xidu, and that day sent Zhen to the capital to work with the chancellors on restoring the throne.
units.literal: He then fixed policy to bind the false envoys Li Fengben, Zhi Yanxun, and Xidu, and that same day asked Zhen to lead the mission to the capital to plot with the chancellors to restore legitimacy.

units.zh: 未幾，劉季述伏誅，昭宗復帝位，太祖聞之喜，召振，執其手謂之曰：「卿所謀是吾本誌，穹蒼其知之矣！」
units.en: Soon Liu Jishu was executed and Zhaozong restored; the Founder rejoiced, summoned Zhen, took his hand and said: "Your plan was always mine—Heaven knows!"
units.literal: Before long Liu Jishu was executed, Zhaozong restored to the throne; the Founder heard and rejoiced, summoned Zhen, took his hand and said: "Your plan is my original intent—Heaven knows!"

units.zh: 自是益重之。
units.en: From then he valued Zhen all the more.
units.literal: From then he valued him all the more.

units.zh: 天祐二年春正月，太祖召振，謂曰：「王師範來降，易歲尚處故藩，今將奏請徙授方面，其為我馳騎，以茲意達之。」
units.en: Tianyou 2, spring month 1, the Founder told Zhen: "Wang Shifan has surrendered but still holds his old domain after nearly a year; I will ask to move him to a new post—ride for me and make that clear."
units.literal: Tianyou 2 spring month 1, the Founder summoned Zhen and said: "Wang Shifan has submitted; nearly a year he still dwells in his old fief; now I will memorialize to transfer him to a circuit commission—ride for me and convey this intent."

units.zh: 振至青州，師範即日出公府，以節度、觀察二印及文簿管鑰授於振。
units.en: At Qingzhou, Shifan left headquarters the same day and gave Zhen the military and surveillance seals, records, and keys.
units.literal: Zhen reached Qingzhou; Shifan that same day left the government hall and handed Zhen the military commissioner and surveillance commissioner seals and documents and keys.

units.zh: 師範雖已受代，而疑撓特甚，屢揮泣求貸其族，振因以切理諭之曰：「公不念張繡事耶！
units.en: Though replaced, Shifan was deeply afraid and wept repeatedly, begging mercy for his clan; Zhen reasoned with him: "Have you forgotten Zhang Xiu!
units.literal: Shifan though already replaced was extremely doubtful and fearful, repeatedly weeping and begging mercy for his clan; Zhen therefore admonished with keen reasoning: "Sir, do you not recall Zhang Xiu's affair!

units.zh: 漢末，繡屢與曹公立敵，豈德之耶，及袁紹遣使招繡，賈詡曰：『袁家父子自不相容，何能主天下英士，曹公挾天子令諸侯，其志大，不以私仇為意，不宜疑之。』
units.en: At the end of Han, Xiu had often fought Lord Cao—would Cao have treated that as a kindness? When Yuan Shao sent envoys to recruit Xiu, Jia Xu said: 'The Yuan father and son cannot abide each other—how could they lead the realm's heroes? Lord Cao holds the Son of Heaven and commands the feudal lords; his aim is great and he does not settle private scores—you should not doubt him.'
units.literal: End of Han, Xiu repeatedly was enemy to Lord Cao—was that virtue? When Yuan Shao sent envoys to recruit Xiu, Jia Xu said: 'The Yuan father and son cannot abide each other—how can they lead the empire's heroes? Lord Cao holds the Son of Heaven and commands the feudal lords; his ambition is great and he does not bear private grudges in mind—you should not doubt him.'

units.zh: 今梁王亦豈以私怨害忠賢耶！」
units.en: Would the King of Liang now destroy loyal men over old grudges!"
units.literal: Today too would the King of Liang harm the loyal and worthy over private grudge!"

units.zh: 師範灑然大悟，翌日，以其族遷。
units.en: Shifan saw the point; the next day he moved his family.
units.literal: Shifan suddenly awakened; next day he moved his clan.

units.zh: 太祖乃表振為青州留後，未幾，征還。
units.en: The Founder made Zhen acting commissioner of Qingzhou, then soon recalled him.
units.literal: The Founder then memorialized Zhen as Qingzhou acting commissioner; before long he was recalled.

units.zh: 唐自昭宗遷都之後，王室微弱，朝廷班行，備員而已。
units.en: After Zhaozong moved the capital the Tang house was feeble and court posts were empty titles.
units.literal: Tang since Zhaozong moved the capital, the royal house was weak; court ranks were mere placeholders.

units.zh: 振皆頤指氣使，旁若無人，朋附者非次獎升，私晉者沈棄。
units.en: Zhen ordered everyone about as if alone in the room; allies rose out of turn and private petitioners were ruined.
units.literal: Zhen everywhere pointed and commanded breath, as if no one else were present; partisans were promoted out of turn, private petitioners were sunk and abandoned.

units.zh: 振每自汴入洛，朝中必有貶竄，故唐朝人士目為「鴟鴞」。
units.en: Whenever Zhen came from Bian to Luoyang someone at court was demoted or exiled—Tang officials called him "the owl."
units.literal: Every time Zhen came from Bian to Luoyang, someone in court was demoted or banished—so Tang court people called him "owl."

units.zh: 天祐中，唐宰相柳璨希太祖旨，譖殺大臣裴樞、陸扆等七人於滑州白馬驛。
units.en: In Tianyou the Tang chancellor Liu Can, courting the Founder, slandered to death seven ministers including Pei Shu and Lu Yi at Baima post in Huazhou.
units.literal: In Tianyou, Tang chief minister Liu Can hoping to please the Founder's intent slandered to death seven great ministers including Pei Shu and Lu Yi at Baima post in Huazhou.

units.zh: 時振自以咸通、乾符中嘗應進士舉，累上不第，尤憤憤，乃謂太祖曰：「此輩自謂清流，宜投於黃河，永為濁流。」
units.en: Zhen had failed the jinshi repeatedly in Xiantong and Qianfu and burned with resentment; he told the Founder: "These men call themselves the Clear Stream—they should be thrown into the Yellow River and be muddy water forever."
units.literal: At that time Zhen himself had in Xiantong and Qianfu repeatedly taken the jinshi examination and repeatedly failed to pass—especially resentful; he told the Founder: "This lot call themselves the Clear Stream—they ought to be thrown into the Yellow River and be the muddy stream forever."

units.zh: 太祖笑而從之。
units.en: The Founder laughed and agreed.
units.literal: The Founder laughed and followed it.

units.zh: 洎太祖受禪，自宣義軍節度副使、檢校司徒授殿中監，累遷戶部尚書。
units.en: When the Founder took the throne, Zhen rose from Xuanyi vice commissioner and honorary Minister of Works to Palace Supervisor and then Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, from Xuanyi army vice commissioner and honorary Minister of Works he was made Palace Supervisor, rising in time to Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 庶人友珪篡立，代敬翔為崇政院使。
units.en: When Yougui seized the throne, Zhen replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.
units.literal: When commoner Yougui usurped the throne, Zhen replaced Jing Xiang as Chongzheng Court commissioner.

units.zh: 末帝即位，趙、張二族用事，遂為所間，謀猷獻替，多不見從，振每稱疾避事。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor the Zhao and Zhang clans ruled; Zhen was sidelined and his counsel was mostly ignored—he often pleaded illness to stay out of affairs.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, the Zhao and Zhang clans held power; he was thus set at odds; stratagems and proposals mostly were not followed—Zhen often claimed illness to avoid affairs.

units.zh: 龍德末，閑居私第將期矣，晉主入汴，振謁見首罪，郭崇韜指振謂人曰：「人言李振乃一代奇才，吾今見之，乃常人耳！」
units.en: At the end of Longde he had lived in retirement nearly a year; when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen came to beg mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at him and said: "They call Li Zhen a wonder of the age—I see an ordinary man!"
units.literal: End of Longde, living in retirement at his private residence nearly a year, when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen paid court asking mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at Zhen and said to people: "People say Li Zhen is a generation's strange talent—I see him now and he is just an ordinary man!"

units.zh: 會段凝等疏梁氏權要之臣，振與敬翔等同日族誅。
units.en: When Duan Ning and others denounced Liang power-holders, Zhen and Jing Xiang were executed to the third degree on the same day.
units.literal: It happened that Duan Ning and others impeached Liang power-holders; Zhen and Jing Xiang were on the same day clan-exterminated.

units.zh: 史臣曰：文蔚、貽矩，皆唐朝之舊臣，遇梁室之強禪，奉君命以來使，狎神器以授之，逢時若斯，亦為臣者之不幸也。
units.en: The historian writes: Zhang Wenyu and Xue Yiju were old Tang ministers; when Liang forced the abdication they came as envoys and casually handed over the throne—in such a time even a loyal minister is unlucky.
units.literal: The historian says: Wenyu and Yiju were all old Tang ministers; encountering the Liang house's forced abdication, they bore the sovereign's command as envoys and familiarly handed over the sacred vessel—to meet such a time is also a minister's misfortune.

units.zh: 抑不為其相，不亦善乎！
units.en: Would it not have been better never to have been their chancellor!
units.literal: Would it not be better not to have been their chancellor!

units.zh: 杜曉著文雅之稱，張策有衝淡之量，鹹登台席，無忝士林。
units.en: Du Xiao had a name for refinement and Zhang Ce for quiet breadth—both reached high office without shaming the scholar class.
units.literal: Du Xiao had the reputation of literary refinement; Zhang Ce had a detached, mild capacity—both ascended the hall and dais without disgracing the scholar class.

units.zh: 敬翔、李振，始輔霸圖，終成帝業。
units.en: Jing Xiang and Li Zhen first helped build the hegemony and in the end helped build the empire.
units.literal: Jing Xiang and Li Zhen at first aided the hegemonic design, in the end accomplished the imperial enterprise.

units.zh: 及國之亡也，一則殞命以明節，一則視息以偷生，以此較之，翔為優矣。
units.en: When the state fell, one died to prove his integrity and one merely breathed on in shame—by that measure Xiang was the better man.
units.literal: When the state perished, one died to clarify integrity, one merely breathed and looked on to steal life—by this comparison Xiang was superior.

units.zh: 振始有濁流之言，終取赤族之禍，報應之事，固以昭然。
units.en: Zhen first spoke of casting men into the muddy stream and in the end suffered extinction of his clan—retribution could hardly be clearer.
units.literal: Zhen at first had the muddy-stream speech, in the end received clan-extinction disaster—retribution's matter is indeed manifest.

units.zh: 況將軍舋非張繡，罪異畢諶，當何慮於危亡，何失於富貴？
units.en: How much more—your rising is not Zhang Xiu's, your crime unlike Bi Chen's—what worry of peril, what loss of wealth and honor?
units.literal: How much more is the general's rising not Zhang Xiu's, his crime unlike Bi Chen's—what worry of peril and extinction, what loss of wealth and honor?

units.zh: 沈炯 虞荔 弟寄 馬樞
units.en: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu
units.literal: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu

units.zh: 甲寅，帝於中興殿麵賜郭崇韜鐵券。
units.en: On jiayin Cunxu personally gave Guo Chongtao an iron tally at Zhongxing Hall.
units.literal: On jiayin the Emperor in person at Zhongxing Hall bestowed on Guo Chongtao an iron tally of mercy.

units.zh: 壬辰，樞密使郭崇韜再上表，請退樞密之職，優詔不允。
units.en: On renchen Guo Chongtao again asked to leave the bureau; Cunxu graciously refused.
units.literal: On renchen Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Guo Chongtao again memorialized asking to resign the bureau post; a gracious edict refused.

units.zh: 樞密使郭崇韜奏時務利便一十五件，優詔褒美。
units.en: Guo Chongtao submitted fifteen reforms; Cunxu praised them.
units.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Guo Chongtao memorialized fifteen items on timely profit and convenience; a gracious edict praised them.

units.zh: 天復元年十一月，宦官韓全誨迫天子幸鳳翔，建亦預其謀。
units.en: Tianfu 1, month 11, Han Quanhui seized the emperor for Fengxiang; Jian helped.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of Tianfu year 1 eunuch Han Quanhui forced the Son of Heaven to go to Fengxiang; Jian also shared the plot.

units.zh: 齊桓公，管仲相之則霸，豎貂輔之則亂。
units.en: Duke Huan of Qi became hegemon when Guan Zhong was his minister, but fell into disorder when Shu Diao aided him.
units.literal: As for Duke Huan of Qi, when Guan Zhong assisted him, he became hegemon; when Shu Diao aided him, there was disorder.

units.zh: 始命韓建為佑國軍節度使。」〉
units.en: Han Jian was first named Youguo Army governor."〉
units.literal: Han Jian was first appointed military governor of the Youguo Army."〉

units.zh: 〈《五代會要》：「四月，改京兆府為大安府，長安縣為大安縣，萬年縣為大年縣，仍置佑國軍節度使額。
units.en: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 records: "In the fourth month Jingzhao became Da'an Prefecture, Chang'an county Da'an, Wannian county Danian, and the Youguo Army post was created.
units.literal: 〈The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》 says: "In the fourth month Jingzhao Prefecture was changed to Da'an Prefecture, Chang'an County to Da'an County, Wannian County to Danian County, and the Youguo Army governorship was established.

units.zh: 乾寧二年，建與鳳翔李茂貞、邠州王行瑜舉兵赴闕，迫昭宗請以王珙為河中帥，害大臣於都下。
units.en: In Qianning 2 Jian joined Li Maozhen of Fengxiang and Wang Xingyu of Binzhou in marching troops to the capital. They pressured Emperor Zhaozong to appoint Wang Gong military governor of Hezhong and killed senior ministers in the capital.
units.literal: In Qianning year 2 Jian with Fengxiang's Li Maozhen and Binzhou's Wang Xingyu raised troops to the capital, forced Zhaozong to make Wang Gong Hezhong commander, and killed great ministers in the capital.

units.zh: 二月甲申，晉王攻我黎陽，劉鄩拒之而退。
units.en: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked Liyang; Liu Xun held him off and forced a withdrawal.
units.literal: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Xun resisted him and drove him back.

units.zh: 貞明三年春正月戊午，以前淄州刺史高允奇為右羽林統軍。
units.en: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
units.literal: On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

units.zh: 乙酉，立皇兄全昱為廣王，皇子友文為博王，友珪為郢王，友璋為福王，友雍為賀王，友徽為建王。
units.en: On yiyou the Emperor enfeoffed his brother Quanyu as Prince of Guang and his sons Youwen, Yougui, Youzhang, Youyong, and Youhui as Princes of Bo, E, Fu, He, and Jian.
units.literal: On yiyou the Emperor's elder brother Quanyu was established as Prince of Guang, the imperial son Youwen as Prince of Bo, Yougui as Prince of E, Youzhang as Prince of Fu, Youyong as Prince of He, and Youhui as Prince of Jian.

units.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；
units.en: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
units.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;

units.zh: 昔陳平背楚，歸漢則強，百里出虞，入秦斯霸。
units.en: Formerly Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he became strong. Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.
units.literal: Formerly Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he became strong. Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.

units.zh: 戊寅，至貝州，命四丞相及學士李琪、盧文度、知制誥竇賞等十五人扈從，其左常侍韋戩等二十三人止焉。
units.en: On wuyin he reached Beizhou and ordered the four chancellors and Academicians Li Qi, Lu Wendu, Drafter Dou Shang, and fifteen others to attend; Left Regular Attendant Wei Zhan and twenty-three others remained behind.
units.literal: On wuyin he reached Beizhou, ordered the four chancellors and Academicians Li Qi, Lu Wendu, Drafter Dou Shang, and fifteen others to attend, while Left Regular Attendant Wei Zhan and twenty-three others remained.

units.zh: 宋州刺史王皋進兩岐麥，陳州袁象先進白兔一，付史館編錄，兼示百官。
units.en: Wang Gao of Songzhou offered double-eared wheat; Yuan Xiangxian of Chenzhou a white hare—both were recorded by the Historiography Office and displayed to the court.
units.literal: Wang Gao, prefect of Songzhou, presented double-eared wheat; Yuan Xiangxian of Chenzhou presented one white hare—both were sent to the Historiography Office for record and shown to the hundred officials.

units.zh: 可改唐天祐四年為開平元年，國號大樑。
units.en: Let Tang's Tianyou year 4 become Kaiping year 1; the realm shall be called Great Liang.
units.literal: Let the fourth year of Tang's Tianyou be changed to the first year of Kaiping; the state name is Great Liang.

units.zh: 靈州奏，鳳翔賊將劉知俊率邠、岐、秦、涇之師侵迫州城。
units.en: Lingzhou reported that Fengxiang rebel Liu Zhijun led Bin, Qi, Qin, and Jing troops against the prefectural seat.
