units.literal: Lingzhou reported that Fengxiang rebel general Liu Zhijun led forces from Bin, Qi, Qin, and Jing to press the prefectural city.

units.zh: 劉知俊攻逼夏州。
units.en: Liu Zhijun pressed Xia Prefecture.
units.literal: Liu Zhijun pressed Xia Prefecture.

units.zh: 初，劉知俊誘沙陀振武賊帥周德威、涇原賊帥李繼鸞合步騎五萬大舉，欲俯拾夏台，節度使李仁福兵力俱乏，以急來告。
units.en: Zhijun had drawn Shatuo Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu and Li Jiluan of Jingyuan with fifty thousand horse and foot, thinking Xia would fall at a touch; Li Renfu was spent and cried for help.
units.literal: Initially Liu Zhijun induced Shatuo Zhenwu rebel leader Zhou Dewei and Jingyuan rebel leader Li Jiluan to combine infantry and cavalry fifty thousand in a great advance, intending to pick up Xia Terrace easily; military governor Li Renfu’s strength was entirely lacking and he reported in urgency.

units.zh: 丙午，詔曰：「劉知俊貴為方伯，尊極郡王，而乃背誕朝恩，竄投賊壘，固神人之共怒，諒天地所不容。
units.en: On bingwu an edict said: "Liu Zhijun was made governor and raised to prince—yet he betrayed the court and fled to rebels; gods and men alike rage and heaven and earth will not hold him.
units.literal: On bingwu an edict stated: "Liu Zhijun was ennobled as regional governor, exalted to prince of a command—yet he betrayed court grace and fled to the rebel camp; surely gods and men jointly rage and Heaven and Earth cannot contain him.

units.zh: 有生擒劉知俊者，賞錢千萬，授節度使，首級次之；
units.en: Whoever takes Zhijun alive gets ten million cash and a military governorship; for his head, the next reward;
units.literal: Whoever captures Liu Zhijun alive—reward ten million cash, appoint military governor; head next in rank;

units.zh: 初，知俊將叛，謀會諸將詢所宜，仁嗣等持正不撓，悉罹其酷，至是褒贈之。
units.en: When Zhijun was plotting revolt he called the generals for counsel; Rensi and the rest stood firm and suffered cruelly—now they were honored in death.
units.literal: When Zhijun was about to rebel he gathered the generals to consult; Rensi and others held firm and upright and all suffered cruelly—now they were posthumously rewarded.

units.zh: 四月，唐帝御劄敕宰臣張文蔚等備法駕奉迎梁朝。
units.en: In the fourth month the Tang emperor sent an imperial decree ordering Zhang Wenwei and the other chief ministers to ready the imperial escort to receive the Liang.
units.literal: In the fourth month, the Tang emperor issued an imperial decree commanding Zhang Wenwei and other chief ministers to prepare the imperial carriage to welcome the Liang court.

units.zh: 又，宰臣張文蔚正押傳國寶、玉冊、金寶及文武群官、諸司儀仗法物及金吾左右二軍離鄭州。
units.en: Chief minister Zhang Wenwei meanwhile led the imperial seal, jade books, gold regalia, the full civil and military establishment, ceremonial equipage of every bureau, and the Left and Right Jinwu guards out of Zhengzhou.
units.literal: Also, chief minister Zhang Wenwei personally escorted the dynastic seal, jade registers, gold seals, civil and military officials of all ranks, ritual regalia of every office, and the Left and Right Jinwu Armies as they departed Zhengzhou.

units.zh: 丙辰，達上源驛。
units.en: On bingchen they arrived at Shangyuan Post.
units.literal: On bingchen they reached Shangyuan Post.

units.zh: 甲辰，天子遣御史大夫薛貽矩來傳禪代之意。
units.en: On jiachen the Son of Heaven sent Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju to convey the plan for abdication.
units.literal: On jiachen the Son of Heaven sent Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju to convey the intention of transferring the mandate.

units.zh: 貽矩謁帝，陳北面之禮，帝揖之升階。
units.en: Yiju called on the Emperor, explained the ceremony of a northern vassal, and the Emperor bowed him up the steps.
units.literal: Yiju called on the Emperor, set forth the rites due a northern vassal, and the Emperor bowed him up the steps.

units.zh: 貽矩曰：「殿下功德及人，三靈所卜已定。
units.en: Yiju said: "Your Highness's merit reaches all men; Heaven, Earth, and the spirits have already settled the matter.
units.literal: Yiju said: "Your Highness's merit reaches all men; the three powers have already decreed the issue.

units.zh: 皇帝方議裁詔，行舜、禹之事，臣安敢違。」
units.en: The emperor is drafting the edict to follow Shun and Yu—I dare not refuse."
units.literal: The emperor is now drafting the edict to do as Shun and Yu did—I dare not disobey."

units.zh: 既而拜伏於砌下，帝側躬以避之。
units.en: He then bowed prostrate on the steps, and the Emperor turned aside.
units.literal: He then bowed prostrate on the steps; the Emperor turned aside to avoid it.

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
units.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
units.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
units.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
units.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
units.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 見嵇康《養生論》，自是歷代未有天下通用如趙過一畝三甽之法者。
units.en: See Ji Kang's Treatise on Nourishing Life; no method since has been applied empire-wide like Zhao Guo's three-furrow-per-mu system.
units.literal: See Ji Kang's "Treatise on Nourishing Life"; from then on through successive dynasties none was universally applied under heaven like Zhao Guo's method of three furrows per mu.

units.zh: 辛未，武安軍節度使馬殷進封楚王。
units.en: On xinwei Ma Yin, governor of the Wu'an Army, was advanced to King of Chu.
units.literal: On xinwei, Ma Yin, military governor of the Wu'an Army, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Chu.

units.zh: 哀帝初嗣位，柳璨用事，全忠嘗奏用牙將張廷範為太常卿，諸相議，樞曰：「廷範勛臣，幸有方鎮節鉞之命，何藉樂卿？
units.en: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized that his guard general Zhang Tingfan be made minister of ceremonies—the chancellors deliberated, and Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister; it would be fitting to grant him a frontier command with military insignia—why need he the post of master of music?
units.literal: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized that his guard general Zhang Tingfan be made Minister of Ceremonies—the chancellors deliberated, and Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister; it would be fitting to grant him a frontier command with military insignia—why need he the post of Master of Music?

units.zh: 柳璨聞全忠言，尋希旨罷樞相位，和陵祔享，拜尚書左僕射。
units.en: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to please him, stripped Shu of the chancellorship; at the joint offering at He-ling, Shu was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to please his intent, removed Shu from the chancellorship; at the joint offering at He-ling, Shu was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 始尚讓以驍騎五千人至繁臺，珍與龐師古、齊奉國等擊退之。
units.en: When Shang Rang brought five thousand horsemen to Fantai, Zhen, Pang Shigu, and Qi Fengguo beat them back.
units.literal: At first Shang Rang came with five thousand fierce cavalry to Fantai; Zhen with Pang Shigu, Qi Fengguo, and others drove him back.
